title: Claude Code Plugin
description: Schema for Claude Code plugin manifest (.claude-plugin/plugin.json). Plugins extend Claude Code with reusable skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, and LSP servers that can be shared across projects and teams. The manifest defines plugin metadata and optionally declares custom component paths. Components in default locations (commands/, agents/, skills/, hooks/hooks.json, .mcp.json, .lsp.json) are auto-discovered even without a manifest. See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference

name.description: Unique identifier for the plugin using lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens (kebab-case, no spaces). This name namespaces all plugin components — skills appear as /plugin-name:skill-name, agents as plugin-name:agent-name, etc. If the manifest is omitted entirely, the directory name is used instead.

version.description: Semantic version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Used to determine when to update installed plugins — if you change code without bumping the version, existing users won't see updates due to caching. If also set in a marketplace entry, the plugin.json version takes priority. Start at 1.0.0 for first stable release.

description.description: Brief explanation of the plugin's purpose. Shown in the plugin manager when browsing or installing plugins.
examples: A greeting plugin to learn the basics

homepage.description: URL to the plugin's documentation or landing page.

repository.description: URL to the plugin's source code repository.

keywords.description: Discovery tags for the plugin. Used when searching or browsing plugins in marketplaces.

commands.description: Additional command file or directory paths, relative to the plugin root starting with './'. These supplement the default commands/ directory — they don't replace it. Paths should point to .md files or directories containing .md files.

agents.description: Additional agent file or directory paths, relative to the plugin root starting with './'. These supplement the default agents/ directory.

skills.description: Additional skill directory paths, relative to the plugin root starting with './'. These supplement the default skills/ directory. Paths should point to directories containing SKILL.md files.

hooks.description: Hook configuration — either paths to JSON config files or inline hook definitions. Custom paths supplement hooks/hooks.json (the default location). Inline definitions map event names to arrays of matcher groups. See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks

oneOf.description: Path to a hooks JSON config file, relative to the plugin root.
Array of paths to hooks JSON config files.

mcpServers.description: MCP server configuration — either paths to JSON config files or inline server definitions. Custom paths supplement .mcp.json (the default location). Inline definitions map server names to their transport configuration. MCP servers start automatically when the plugin is enabled. See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp

oneOf.description: Path to an MCP config JSON file, relative to the plugin root.
Array of paths to MCP config JSON files.
Inline MCP server definitions. Each key is a server name and the value is either a string reference to an already-configured server or a full server configuration object.
Reference to an already-configured MCP server by name.

outputStyles.description: Additional output style files or directories, relative to the plugin root starting with './'.

lspServers.description: LSP server configuration — either paths to JSON config files or inline server definitions. Custom paths supplement .lsp.json (the default location). Inline definitions map language names to their server configuration, providing Claude with real-time code intelligence (diagnostics, go to definition, find references). Users must install the language server binary separately. See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference#lsp-servers

oneOf.description: Path to an LSP config JSON file, relative to the plugin root.
Array of paths to LSP config JSON files.
Inline LSP server definitions. Each key is a language name and the value is a server configuration object.
A single relative path starting with './'.
Array of relative paths, each starting with './'.

McpServerConfig.description: Inline MCP server definition with transport configuration.

command.description: Executable to run for the MCP server. Use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} for plugin-relative paths.

args.description: Arguments to pass to the command.

env.description: Environment variables for the server process. Values support ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}.

cwd.description: Working directory for the server process.

LspServerConfig.description: LSP server configuration for a language. The language server binary must be installed separately on the user's machine.

command.description: The LSP binary to execute (must be in PATH).

extensionToLanguage.description: Maps file extensions to language identifiers.

args.description: Command-line arguments for the LSP server.

env.description: Environment variables to set when starting the server.

initializationOptions.description: Options passed to the server during initialization.

workspaceFolder.description: Workspace folder path for the server.

startupTimeout.description: Max time to wait for server startup in milliseconds.

shutdownTimeout.description: Max time to wait for graceful shutdown in milliseconds.

restartOnCrash.description: Whether to automatically restart the server if it crashes.

maxRestarts.description: Maximum number of restart attempts before giving up.

Hooks.description: Map of event names to arrays of matcher groups. Each matcher group optionally filters by a regex pattern and contains an array of hook handlers that execute when the event fires.

SessionStart.description: Fires when a session starts. Matcher filters by session source: 'startup' (new session), 'resume' (resuming previous session), 'clear' (after /clear), 'compact' (after context compaction). Command hooks have access to $CLAUDE_ENV_FILE for persisting environment variables across the session.

UserPromptSubmit.description: Fires when the user submits a prompt, before Claude processes it. No matcher support — always fires on every user message. Hooks can block the prompt (preventing Claude from seeing it) or modify it before processing.

PreToolUse.description: Fires before a tool is executed. Matcher filters by tool name (e.g. 'Bash', 'Edit|Write', 'mcp__.*'). Hooks can block the tool call (exit code 2 or {ok: false}), modify its input via hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput, auto-allow/deny permission via hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision ('allow', 'deny', 'ask'), or inject additional context via hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext.

PermissionRequest.description: Fires when a tool requests user permission before executing. Matcher filters by tool name. Hooks can auto-allow or deny the permission via hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior ('allow' or 'deny'), optionally modifying the tool input via decision.updatedInput or updating permissions via decision.updatedPermissions. If denied, decision.message is shown to the user.

PostToolUse.description: Fires after a tool executes successfully. Matcher filters by tool name. Hooks can inject additional context for Claude via hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext (e.g. lint results after a file write) or replace MCP tool output via hookSpecificOutput.updatedMCPToolOutput. Supports async hooks that run in the background without blocking.

PostToolUseFailure.description: Fires after a tool execution fails. Matcher filters by tool name. Hooks can inject additional context to help Claude understand and recover from the failure. Supports async hooks.

Notification.description: Fires on notifications. Matcher filters by type: 'permission_prompt', 'idle_prompt', 'auth_success', 'elicitation_dialog'.

SubagentStart.description: Fires when a subagent is spawned. Matcher filters by agent type.

SubagentStop.description: Fires when a subagent stops. Matcher filters by agent type.

Stop.description: Fires when Claude's turn ends and it is about to stop. No matcher support — always fires. Hooks can force Claude to continue working by returning {continue: false} with a reason.

TeammateIdle.description: Fires when a teammate goes idle. No matcher support — always fires.

TaskCompleted.description: Fires when a task is marked completed. No matcher support — always fires.

PreCompact.description: Fires before context compaction. Matcher filters by trigger type: 'manual', 'auto'.

SessionEnd.description: Fires when a session ends. Matcher filters by exit reason: 'clear', 'logout', 'prompt_input_exit', 'bypass_permissions_disabled', 'other'.

MatcherGroup.description: A matcher group pairs an optional regex filter with an array of hook handlers. If matcher is omitted, the hooks fire on every occurrence of the event.

matcher.description: Regex pattern to filter when this group's hooks fire. Use '|' for OR (e.g. 'Edit|Write'), '.*' for wildcards (e.g. 'mcp__.*'). MCP tools follow the pattern mcp__<server>__<tool>. Omit to match all.

CommandHook.description: Runs a shell command or script synchronously (or async if configured). The command receives hook context as JSON on stdin, including session_id, transcript_path, cwd, permission_mode, hook_event_name, and event-specific fields. Exit code 0 means success — stdout is parsed as JSON and can contain fields like 'continue' (boolean), 'stopReason' (string), 'systemMessage' (string), and event-specific 'hookSpecificOutput'. Exit code 2 is a blocking error — stderr is fed to Claude as an error message. Any other exit code is a non-blocking error logged in verbose mode.

command.description: Shell command or script path to execute. The command runs in the project's working directory. Use $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR for the project root (always quote it: "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/path) and ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} for plugin-relative paths.

statusMessage.description: Spinner message while the hook runs.

async.description: Run in background without blocking. Only supported for PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure events.

once.description: Run once per session then remove.

PromptHook.description: Evaluates a single-turn LLM prompt to make a pass/fail decision. A small, fast model receives the prompt and must respond with {ok: true} to allow the action, or {ok: false, reason: 'explanation'} to block it. Cannot use tools — decides based solely on the prompt content. Best for quick validation checks like safety screening or format verification.

prompt.description: The evaluation prompt sent to the LLM. Use $ARGUMENTS to interpolate the hook's full input context as JSON, including session_id, cwd, tool_name, tool_input, and other event-specific fields.
examples: Is this Bash command safe to run? Review for destructive operations: $ARGUMENTS
Does this file edit follow our coding standards? $ARGUMENTS

model.description: Model for evaluation. Defaults to a fast model for low latency.

statusMessage.description: Spinner message while the hook runs.

once.description: Run once per session then remove.

AgentHook.description: Runs a multi-turn LLM agent that can use tools (Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, etc.) to gather additional context before making a decision. Unlike prompt hooks, agent hooks can explore the codebase and run commands to verify conditions. Must respond with {ok: true} or {ok: false, reason: 'explanation'}. Best for complex validations requiring file reads or external checks.

prompt.description: The verification prompt sent to the agent. Use $ARGUMENTS to interpolate the hook's full input context as JSON. The agent can then use tools to investigate further before deciding.
examples: Verify this MCP write operation is valid and won't cause data loss: $ARGUMENTS

model.description: Model for the agent. Defaults to a fast model.

statusMessage.description: Spinner message while the hook runs.

once.description: Run once per session then remove.
